run_context: This run followed a capped (131,072-context) attempt on pod-qwen that was killed WITHOUT scoring after infra decided to relaunch uncapped (see _runs/_extra-capped-131k or _invalid-capped-131k for that discarded attempt -- it does not count toward any result). This scored run used pod-qwen-medium (medium effort) on the restarted Qwen-A server at --max-model-len 262144 (models.yml contextWindow 262144, confirmed at launch time). It did not complete naturally: the opening turn (turn 0, general exploration/research, not a milestone) ran the full 4-hour per-turn guard and was force-aborted (turn-0.json's final event: stopReason='aborted', errorMessage='Deadline exceeded', matching the same shape as an earlier radix/qwen-r2 guard-hit). Turn 1 (the M1 milestone turn) then started immediately at 03:45:51 EDT and ran until the pod's scheduled 04:55/04:57 EDT hard stop terminated it mid-turn; the harness was left retrying against the now-dead server and had to be finalized manually by the queue-runner, which appended 'turn 1 rc=cut (pod terminated 04:57 EDT at the spend hard stop; turns 2-5 not attempted)' and 'DONE raptor/qwen' to driver.log at 05:42:10 EDT. Turns 2-5 (M2-M5) never started. Per the pre-committed contingency, this partial run is scored exactly as it stands, with unreached milestones marked as not attempted rather than failed.

milestones.label: renders level + ship
milestones.notes: M1 was implemented and committed (0005fbadbaa652b89c30967d96d1f52f56102ca6, 'M1: level-1 background + player ship from real GLB data', 2026-08-21 04:47:23 EDT -- 3692s after turn 1 started at 03:45:51). The model's own tasks/todo.md marks M1 done and says 'Verified headless (scripts/smoke.js -> PNG)'. However M1 FAILS the acceptance check, and for a real, reproducible reason: js/game.js allocates one reusable ImageData buffer at load time (`const img = ctx.createImageData(W, H)`, W=320 H=200 = 64,000 pixels) and sets its alpha channel with `for (let i = 0; i < 256; i++) { px[i*4+3] = 255; }` -- an off-by-a-lot bound (256 instead of W*H=64000) that leaves 63,744 of the canvas's 64,000 pixels at alpha=0 (fully transparent) for the entire session; only the first 256 pixels (less than one scanline) are ever made opaque. The RGB color computation itself runs correctly every frame (present()'s per-pixel loop writes real r/g/b for all 64,000 pixels from the game's own screen buffer and palette), so the underlying render logic is not obviously broken -- but because almost the entire canvas stays transparent, essentially nothing is visually rendered: a page screenshot shows solid black (the page background showing through), and a direct canvas.toDataURL() capture (bypassing the page background, capturing the raw buffer as DSV4's M1 capture script does) shows a near-blank frame with a short opaque sliver in the top-left corner. Confirmed via direct getImageData() sampling in headless Chromium (multiple sample points at alpha=0, only pixel (0,0) at alpha=255) -- not a checker artifact. SSIM/palette were measured against the correct capture (canvas.toDataURL, matching DSV4's own M1 methodology), not a full-page screenshot. This is scored as a straightforward M1 FAIL; the bug was not fixed for scoring purposes (checker/scorer never edits model code).

Architecture note: unlike dsv4 (which decodes the two GLB archives at runtime via fetch()), this build pre-decodes everything at build time into js/assets.js (a 31,992-line generated file of base64-embedded asset data) via scripts/build.js, so the shipped runtime (js/game.js) makes no network/file requests at all.
